does: Chops parsley very fine with lemon zest and a little raw garlic, to be scattered over a rich, slow-cooked dish at the very end, where its sharp freshness cuts through the fat. Nothing is cooked.

intro.what: Gremolata finely chops parsley, lemon zest and raw garlic into a fresh finish.
intro.why: It teaches you to add contrast to a rich dish without cooking away the bright scent of the garnish.

how: Pick the parsley leaves from the stalks and dry them well.
Grate the zest of the lemon in fine strips, taking only the yellow.
Peel the garlic and chop it fine with the parsley, then chop in the zest, until everything is small and even.
Make it just before serving and scatter it over the dish at the table, and not into the pot.

cues.text: Bright lemon and green parsley, with a sharp edge of garlic.
The mix is fine and even and still bright green.

mistakes.mistake: Grating in the white pith, which tastes bitter.
mistakes.fix: Take only the yellow of the peel.

mistakes.mistake: Mixing it into the pot early, so that it loses its freshness and turns dull.
mistakes.fix: Scatter it over the dish at the very end.

mistakes.mistake: Chopping wet parsley, which turns to a paste.

quiz.question: What does gremolata bring to a rich dish?
choices: A sharp, fresh contrast at the end.
A thick sauce cooked into the pot.
quiz.because: Fresh parsley, lemon and garlic finish the dish with a bright contrast.

quiz.question: Which part of the lemon peel should you grate?
choices: The white pith beneath the zest.
A thick shaving containing all the pith.
The yellow zest without the white pith.
quiz.because: The yellow zest supplies the lemon scent without the bitter white pith.

quiz.question: Which appearance matches freshly made gremolata?
choices: Fine, even pieces that are still bright green.
A dull green paste dissolved into the sauce.
Large wet parsley clumps with white pith.
quiz.because: Dry leaves and fine chopping preserve a bright, even finishing mixture.

quiz.question: The gremolata loses freshness after cooking in the pot. What would you change next time?
choices: Add it before the slow cooking begins.
Scatter it over the dish at the very end.
Cook it separately until the parsley darkens.
quiz.because: Early cooking dulls the fresh finish; add it at serving instead.

comes_after.why: The parsley is chopped small and even, and a cook has to be able to chop first.
